title: Quality Information Disclosure and Patient Reallocation in the Healthcare Industry: Evidence from Cardiac Surgery Report Cards
eligible_reason: Single event (first New Jersey CABG report cards, November 1997) in a single state with no control states; patient-level discrete-choice (conditional logit) models with hospital FE interacted with pre/post periods.
design_notes: Author states (Sec. 5) that a DiD would be appropriate only if data from other states were available as a control group, which they are not; identification is within-NJ pre/post (report-card publication) with patient-urgency heterogeneity, plus border vs non-border hospital comparison and a survival-quality analysis with half-year FE. NY and PA also had report cards and are not used as controls. Estimation is nonlinear (choice model) with patient-urgency x policy interactions.
estimators_reported: logit risk model with surgeon and half-year FE
screener_notes: Not eligible: single adoption date, no untreated comparison unit, nonlinear choice model, subgroup-by-policy interactions. No replication package was listed in the batch file (package_dir and regressions_path empty); screening is from the article text only. Data: New Jersey Dept of Health CABG discharge data and Open Heart Surgery Registry (provided by NJDOH) plus HCUP SID; restricted.
